disposition: No demonstrated 3D layout or unreachable-primary-action defect in the assigned evidence. Intended scrolling accounts for the captured clipping. No code proposal warranted.

findings.finding: Show hand is fully visible outside the scrollable body. Initial offscreen cards and disabled Select cards do not block the required reveal action.

Large text scale creates separate text card selectors. Reveal requests the first selector into view after layout. Source scroll/focus restoration and a scrolled selected capture explain the artwork cut at the scroll boundary.

The scrollable body orders named results and match words before a 220-unit-minimum artwork stage and continuation/return controls. Thirteen round advances each used one retained native drag; final return used two and reached CLOSED/RETURN_TO_LOBBY.

Continuation is initially below the result viewport, with a visible scrollbar and successful native scrolling recorded. The evidence does not establish a primary-action discoverability defect; no human usability claim is made.
